messages:
jules: Hey — BrightLane reports repeated 429s in prod since 09:12 UTC. They claim they are under their published quota but seeing ~3k requests/min spikes from their ingest job. Sample: curl -> 429 with Retry-After: 1. Can someone triage?

support-eng: Can you paste the full response headers + the org id and route? Also which model/route? If you have a request_id that helps.

jules: Org=brightlane-prod, route=/v1/generate, model=redwood-small, req_id=rcq-0b7f. Headers:
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 1
X-RateLimit-Limit-RPM: 600
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 14
X-Region: us-west-2

ingest-monitor: alert: org=brightlane-prod high 429 rate (10m avg 47% of requests 429). See: https://logs.internal/rcq-0b7f

marco: Interesting — X-RateLimit-Limit-RPM shows 600. Is that per-route or per-org? BrightLane purchased 10k RPM but maybe only applied to embeddings or a different plan. support-eng, confirm billing tier?

support-eng: Billing shows BrightLane on Standard tier with 10k monthly/minute? Hmm config says default per-route caps still at 600 RPM for /v1/generate. I'll open a config check.

sre-oncall: Two quick checks: 1) Are their client instances multiplexing connections? 2) Are their timestamps aligned to our minute windows? If they fan out many short-lived clients, each can create minute boundary stamp issues and create spikes within our per-minute buckets.

jules: They have 12 ingestion workers in k8s, each spinning batches every 5s. Repro script attached below:
for i in {1..12}; do while true; do curl -s -w "\n%{http_code}\n" -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate & sleep 0.2; done & done

support-eng: That script will create very bursty microbursts. Recommend adding jitter and smoothing, or use batched requests. Short-term we can increase route cap to 2k RPM for next 24h while they refactor.

marco: I can patch a temporary override but need approval from product ops. Also check if this is across regions — if they use multi-region failover their requests might hit different buckets.

ingest-team: Also check client retry logic — they should respect Retry-After and avoid immediate retries. Some SDKs retry aggressively on non-200 and can amplify.

dev-bot: link to playbook: https://go.internal/playbooks/429-troubleshoot

support-eng: Plan: (1) Ask BrightLane to run non-bursty test with single worker 60s. (2) Apply temporary route override 24h -> 2000 RPM and monitor. (3) If fixes, schedule quota increase or advise batching + jitter. Ticket INC-7834 opened and assigned to marco.

jules: Sent customer the 60s test, they agreed. I'll update when they finish. Thanks :thumbsup:

sre-oncall: FYI — we'll also add a note to docs about per-route caps vs overall org quota to avoid future confusion.
